extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and IPO/patent office staff preparing ST.26 sequence listings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding which nucleotide and amino‑acid sequences must or may be included in a WIPO ST.26-compliant sequence listing, how to interpret nonconventional/ambiguous symbols, and how to represent/annotate sequences and modified residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide inclusion threshold (Paragraph 6(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear portions of nucleotide sequences containing ten or more specifically defined nucleotides, wherein adjacent nucleotides are joined 3' to 5', must be included in a sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to linear segments of branched nucleic acids (e.g., vertical branches B–E included, horizontal branch A excluded in comb-type example). If a linear portion has ≥10 specifically defined nucleotides joined 3'→5' include it as a sequence with its own SEQ ID. Relevant paragraphs: 6(a), 7, 10, 13, 17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino-acid inclusion threshold (Paragraph 6(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Peptides containing four or more specifically defined amino acids must be included in a sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count specifically defined amino acids even if interspersed with 'X' or ambiguity symbols; include unbranched/linear portions of branched peptides that contain ≥4 defined residues as separate SEQ IDs. Example: peptides 1–6 in a branched Lys-scaffold must be included. Relevant paragraphs: 6(b), 25, 29, 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including sequences below thresholds (Paragraph 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence listing must not include any sequences having fewer than ten specifically defined nucleotides (for nucleotide sequences) or fewer than four specifically defined amino acids (for peptide sequences) as separate sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an enumerated sequence expands (after interpreting nonconventional symbols) to fewer than the applicable threshold it cannot be included as a separate sequence. Exception: a disclosed alternative sequence that explicitly defines residues to reach the threshold may be included (example: replace some 'n' with adenine to reach ≥10). CAUTION: representations acceptable at filing date may not be acceptable later if they add subject matter. Relevant paragraphs: 7, 6(a), 6(b), example 6(a)-6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of nonconventional symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: When a symbol used in an enumerated sequence might be conventional or nonconventional, consult the disclosure to determine its meaning; if used in a nonconventional manner it must be interpreted as the equivalent conventional symbols for inclusion/representation purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Xaa used nonconventionally → interpret positions as Lys/Gly/Leu/Ile and use K/G/J; 'MDR' expanded to ATTTTTTAT; 'N' or 'β' defined as a specific 9-mer → expand to conventional symbols; Ψ (pseudouridine) → interpret as 'n' with modified_base annotation. Relevant paragraphs: Introduction, 3(h), 13, examples 3(h)-5, 6(a)-3, 6(a)-4, 6(a)-5, 6(a)-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most restrictive ambiguity symbol (Paragraph 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: When shorthand/formula variables (e.g., z) are defined only as 'any amino acid', the most restrictive conventional ambiguity symbol should be used in the listing (i.e., 'X' for 'any amino acid').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand formulas first, then determine variables. If a variable is the same across occurrences and that constraint is disclosed, use a VARIANT feature with NOTE to indicate that the X positions must be identical. Examples: (GGGz)2 → GGGXGGGX; if z must be same amino acid, add VARIANT/NOTE. Relevant paragraphs: 3(bbis), 6(b), 25, 26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence representation direction and SEQ ID assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sequence included in the listing must be represented in the 5'→3' direction (for nucleotides) and assigned its own sequence identification number; for double-stranded fully complementary sequences at least one strand must be included, but both may be included as separate SEQ IDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including both strands, represent each in 5'→3' orientation and assign separate SEQ ID numbers (examples SEQ ID NO: 34–35). For non-standard constructs follow direction rules specified in Paragraph 10. Relevant paragraphs: 6(a), 10(a), 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-stranded sequences that are not fully complementary
rubrics_metrics.description: If the two strands are not fully complementary, both strands must be included in the sequence listing, each with its own SEQ ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a genomic promoter (top strand) and a PNA probe (bottom strand) not fully complementary must both be listed. Represent each strand in the 5'→3' direction; PNA has special representation rules (see PNA criterion). Relevant paragraphs: 10(b), 3(d), 6(a), 13, 17, 17bis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branched nucleotide sequences — include linear branches and annotate
rubrics_metrics.description: For branched (comb-type) nucleic acids include each linear branch that contains ≥10 specifically defined nucleotides joined 3'→5' as separate sequences; linear portions linked by non-nucleotide moieties with fewer than ten nucleotides are not required and must not be separate sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate branch origin using feature_key 'misc_feature' and a 'note' qualifier (e.g., 'This sequence is one of four branches of a branched polynucleotide'). Identical branches may be included as a single sequence with annotation. Relevant paragraphs: 6(a), 7, 10, 13, 17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branched amino-acid sequences — include linear portions and annotate cross-links
rubrics_metrics.description: In branched peptides, include unbranched/linear portions that contain four or more specifically defined amino acids as separate sequences and note cross-linking sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign separate SEQ IDs to each included peptide segment. Indicate cross-links using feature_key 'SITE' with mandatory qualifier 'NOTE' (e.g., 'This sequence is one part of a branched peptide'). Annotate modified amino acids where applicable. Relevant paragraphs: 6(b), 25, 29, 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation of modified or non-standard residues (feature keys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified bases and non-standard residues must be annotated in the feature table using the appropriate feature keys and qualifiers (e.g., 'modified_base' with 'mod_base' value, 'misc_feature', 'misc_difference').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: pseudouridine (Ψ) mapped to 'n' and described with feature_key 'modified_base' and mod_base 'p'; thymine in RNA represented as 't' must be described with modified_base/OTHER and a 'note' 'thymine'; if positions may be substituted with modified bases use 'misc_difference' with note and 'modified_base' entries. See Annex I feature key examples (feature key 5.42 etc.). Relevant paragraphs: 6(a), 10, 13, 14, 62, 85, Annex I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and annotation of PNA and other synthetic constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Peptide nucleic acids (PNA) and similar constructs are considered nucleotides for ST.26 and, if they contain ten or more specifically defined residues, must be included and annotated appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent PNA sequences 'left-to-right' mimicking 5'→3' direction (since PNA lacks 3'/5' ends). Use 'source' qualifier 'organism' = 'synthetic construct' and mandatory 'mol_type' = 'other DNA'. Describe modified residues with 'modified_base' and mod_base 'OTHER' and include a 'note' with the full unabbreviated name (e.g., 'N-(2-aminoethyl) glycine nucleosides'). Relevant paragraphs: 3(d), 6(a), 10(b), 17, 17bis.

rubrics_metrics.name: RNA representation rules (Paragraph 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: In sequence listings, 'u' cannot be used for uracil; the symbol 't' is construed as uracil in RNA. Thymine appearing in an RNA molecule is considered a modified uracil and must be represented as 't' and further described in the feature table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an RNA segment containing Ψ or thymine must be included with 't' where appropriate and any thymine/modified residue annotated using 'modified_base' with mod_base 'OTHER' and a 'note' describing the modification (e.g., 'thymine'). Also use 'misc_feature' note describing attachments/linkers when present. Relevant paragraphs: 3(d), 6(a), 7, 13, 14, 18, 54.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encoded-protein/terminator handling and CDS annotation (Paragraph 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide sequence that encodes translated proteins and contains internal terminator symbols must be included as a single nucleotide sequence if it has >10 nucleotides; the encoded amino-acid sequences separated by internal terminators must be included as separate sequences if each contains ≥4 amino acids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each encoded protein include a 'CDS' feature, with INSDFeature_location identifying the coding region including stop codon; include 'translation' qualifier with the amino-acid sequence, include 'transl_table' qualifier if a nonstandard genetic code applies, and include 'protein_id' indicating the SEQ ID of the protein sequence. Relevant paragraphs: 27, Annex 1 Section 9 Table 5, 6(a), 6(b), 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific feature keys and qualifiers (Annex I guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings must use the standard feature keys and qualifiers (e.g., 'source' with 'organism' and 'mol_type', 'misc_feature', 'modified_base', 'misc_difference', 'SITE', 'VARIANT', 'CDS', 'translation', 'transl_table', 'protein_id') and the mandatory/appropriate qualifier values required by ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the guidance show when to use each key/qualifier and sample values/notes (e.g., 'mol_type' = 'tRNA' for tRNA sequences; 'mod_base' values 'p' for pseudouridine or 'OTHER' with a 'note' giving full name). Follow Annex I Table definitions for feature keys and qualifiers. Relevant paragraphs: Annex I, feature key tables, multiple examples throughout document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling ambiguous/nonconventional symbols that reduce sequence below threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: If nonconventional symbols in a sequence, once interpreted as conventional symbols, lead to fewer than the required specifically defined residues, the sequence cannot be included; however, disclosed specific alternatives that reach the threshold may be included with appropriate annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 5' GATC-β-β-β-β-GTAC where β = adenine/inosine/pseudouridine → interpreted as NNNN giving only 8 defined nucleotides and thus cannot be included; but an alternative where at least 2 'n' positions are replaced by A to reach ≥10 is allowed (annotate substitutions with misc_difference and modified_base entries). CAUTION re: adding subject matter if altering representation after filing. Relevant paragraphs: 6(a), 7, 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferential inclusion of most-encompassing embodiments and caution on subject-matter addition
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple embodiments are disclosed (e.g., repeats with variable n), prefer including the most-encompassing explicitly disclosed sequence (e.g., maximum repeat length) and annotate deletions/variants, but be cautious because representations acceptable on the filing date may not be appropriate later if they would add subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for (Gly-Gly-Gly-z)n with n=2–100, preferred to include sequence with 100 copies and annotate possible deletions; also include representative shorter sequences (2,3 copies) where appropriate. CAUTION: representation preference applies to listing at filing date; later listings may be restricted. Relevant paragraphs: 3(bbis), 6(b), 25, 26.
